rule: This file owns the closed conflict-class vocabulary for workspace integration, and nothing else. A class is admitted here only when the controller can compute it from facts it already records, and every class names those facts in `observable_from`; a class nothing observes would be a class an agent could assert rather than derive, which is the opposite of what this vocabulary is for. `NO_CONFLICT` is a member because a classification has to be total - the controller must be able to say that it looked and found nothing - and it is never a refusal reason, because a refusal citing it would say both that there is a conflict and that there is none. Every other class is a refusal reason. The vocabulary is owned here; schemas/workspace-v1/admission.schema.json and the constants in crates/storage/src/lib.rs restate it, and the contract gate fails if any of the three stops agreeing with the other two.

NO_CONFLICT.meaning: Every candidate's changed paths are disjoint from the others' and from the protected set, no candidate touches a contract artifact or a dependency manifest, and every candidate's base checkpoint, epoch and context digest are the current ones. This is the value that says nothing was found.

PATH_OVERLAP.meaning: Two or more candidates in one integration touch the same path. Paths are recorded in full as strings, so this is computable without reading any file's contents.

PROTECTED_PATH.meaning: A candidate touches a path the workspace policy marks protected, or the protected-path set could not be determined at all. The class is computed from the checks as well as from the paths because an undetermined protected set is not the same fact as a clean one, and treating it as clean is how a protected write gets admitted.

SCHEMA_OR_CONTRACT_FILE_CONFLICT.meaning: Two or more candidates change the same contract artifact - a schema, a declared registry or a generated surface. The repository gives each of those exactly one owner, so two concurrent changes to one of them cannot both be the owner's intent, and the paths alone are enough to see it.

DEPENDENCY_MANIFEST_CONFLICT.meaning: Two or more candidates change a dependency manifest, so the dependency set resolved after integration is not the set either candidate was validated against. Each candidate may pass its own checks and the integrated result still be untested.

STALE_BASE.meaning: A candidate's base checkpoint is not the workspace's current one, or its epoch or context digest no longer matches. The work was produced against a state that no longer exists, so integrating it would merge a change whose effect was never observed in the state it lands in.

POST_MERGE_VALIDATION_FAILURE.meaning: The integration succeeded and validation of the integrated result then failed. This is attribution after the fact rather than a pre-merge prediction: it is recorded because the integration that produced it is the thing that failed, and no pre-merge class could have named it. It may only be cited by an INTEGRATION_ADMISSION, because only an integration record describes an integration that happened.

TEXT_CONFLICT.reason: A textual merge conflict is the outcome of attempting a merge, and nothing in this repository observes hunks or line ranges: `changed_paths` holds whole path strings, no table stores a diff, no merge is performed anywhere, and rollback_workspace is contract-declared but implemented in no crate. A class the controller cannot compute would be a class an agent could assert, which is exactly what a controller-computed classification exists to prevent. The class becomes admissible here the moment hunk-level data is recorded; until then its absence is the honest statement, and it is recorded rather than left to be noticed.
